name: Mounting Points (Lift, Tow, Rivnuts, Tabs)
description: Body hard points used for lifting/jacking, towing/recovery, and attaching lines, harnesses and small brackets: factory pinch-weld lift points, tow-eye receptacles, plus rivnuts and weld-on tabs added during the build.

components.name: Lift and jacking points (rocker pinch welds)
components.description: Factory lift points on the rocker pinch-weld flanges just behind the front wheel openings and just ahead of the rear wheel openings. Use these for 2-post lifts and jack stands. For pit-lane jacking a race car normally uses a center front jacking point (front cradle or a dedicated jack plate) and a rear point at the rear cradle front crossmember/braces.
components.location: Rocker underside approx (x 0.55, y 0.14, z +/-0.86) and (x 2.35, y 0.14, z +/-0.86).

factory.name: GM pinch-weld lift points (marked by notches/arrows on rocker cover)
factory.notes: Gen 6 owner's manual shows jack locations at the rocker pinch welds; do not lift on the plastic rocker moldings or on suspension links.

raceOptions.name: Weld-on jack pads / pinch-weld jack pad adapters
raceOptions.notes: A welded tubular jacking point at each rocker or a center jack plate on the front cradle allows fast pit-lane lifts with a racing jack.

installNotes: Weld any custom jacking points during phase 1 before paint.
Mark the points with paint so crew can find them.
inspection: Check pinch welds for crush damage.

modelRef.features: Pinch-weld lift points with rubber jack pads

components.name: Front tow-eye receptacle and race tow strap
components.description: Threaded receptacle in the front bumper beam/crush can (accessed through a fascia cover) for the factory screw-in tow eye. Race sanctioning bodies require an accessible, clearly marked tow point at front and rear; most racers install a fabric tow strap bolted to the bumper beam or frame rail tip.
components.location: Sleeve on the front bumper-beam face, right of centre, behind the fascia tow cover: x -0.729 to -0.693, y 0.475, z -0.47.

factory.name: GM screw-in tow eye (stored with jack kit)
factory.notes: Check the owner's manual for thread direction before forcing - some GM tow eyes use reverse threads.

raceOptions.name: Bolt-on nylon tow strap
raceOptions.notes: Bolt to the bumper beam / rail tip with a grade 10.9 bolt and large washer; must not interfere with splitter or ducts. Colour must contrast with the body per most rulebooks.

hardware.spec: M10 or M12 x 1.25 flange bolt with fender washer (match receptacle)
hardware.notes: Generic metric 10.9 values - verify receptacle thread.

installNotes: Mount strap so it pulls in line with the rail; route outside the splitter edge.
inspection: Check strap for fraying and mounting bolt tightness each event.

modelRef.features: Threaded tow-eye boss with a race tow strap

components.name: Rear tow point
components.description: Rear tow eye receptacle / rear tow strap mounted to the rear rail or rear bumper beam. Must be reachable without removing bodywork and must clear the diffuser and exhaust.
components.location: Sleeve through the rear bumper beam, left of centre, ending behind the rear fascia tow opening: x 3.725-3.792, y 0.50, z 0.30.

factory.name: GM rear tow eye receptacle (screw-in eye)

hardware.spec: M10 or M12 flange bolt with fender washer (match receptacle)

modelRef.features: Threaded tow point with tow strap

components.name: Front bumper beam and crush cans
components.description: Swept aluminium bumper beam behind the front fascia, between the intercooler heat exchanger and the radiator, bolted to two crush cans on the front frame-rail tips. It carries the front tow-eye sleeve and the upper splitter hanger tabs.
components.location: Inside the front fascia: beam x -0.735 to -0.66, y 0.435-0.515, z +/-0.56; crush cans x -0.675 to -0.59 at z +/-0.465.

factory.name: GM extruded aluminium front bumper beam with bolt-on crush cans
factory.notes: Crush cans bolt to the rail-tip flanges with 4 nuts each.

installNotes: Fit the beam before the fascia; check the tow-eye sleeve lines up with the fascia tow cover.
inspection: Check the crush cans for buckling after any front contact.

modelRef.dimensions: beam approx 45 x 80 mm section, 1.12 m wide; crush cans approx 85 x 75 mm
modelRef.features: Swept beam, two crush cans with flanges, splitter hanger tabs

components.name: Rear bumper beam and crush cans
components.description: Steel rear bumper beam behind the rear fascia, bolted to short crush cans on the rear-rail tips. It carries the rear tow sleeve.
components.location: Inside the rear fascia: beam x 3.66-3.74, y 0.45-0.55, z +/-0.52; crush cans x 3.605-3.668 at z +/-0.485.

factory.name: GM rear bumper beam with bolt-on crush cans

installNotes: Fit the beam before the rear fascia; line the tow sleeve up with the fascia tow opening.
inspection: Check the crush cans for buckling after any rear contact.

modelRef.dimensions: beam approx 50 x 100 mm section, 1.04 m wide
modelRef.features: Beam with two crush cans and flanges

components.name: Rivnuts / nutserts for line, harness and bracket mounting
components.description: Steel threaded insert rivets installed into body sheet metal to give removable mounting points for brake/fuel line clamps, harness P-clips, fire-system lines, ducting, splash shields and panels without access to the back side. Use steel (not aluminum) rivnuts in structural or vibrating locations; avoid installing them in rail walls, datum holes or crush zones.
components.location: Throughout: tunnel and floor (line runs), firewall, inner fenders, trunk floor.

factory.name: Factory weld studs and clip holes (partially reusable)
factory.notes: Many factory line clips snap onto weld studs; reuse where routing matches.

raceOptions.name: Steel ribbed rivnuts M5/M6 (or 10-24 / 1/4-20)
raceOptions.notes: Hex-body rivnuts resist spinning better than round-body in thin sheet.

specs.Typical sizes: M5 and M6 in 0.7-1.5 mm sheet
specs.Install: Hand or pneumatic rivnut tool, correct grip range

hardware.item: Screw into M6 steel rivnut (P-clip/line clamp)
hardware.notes: Per fastener; over-torque spins the rivnut.

installNotes: Lay out every line and harness route (phase 2/8) and mark clip positions every 300-400 mm before drilling.
Drill to exact rivnut size, deburr, prime the bare edge (weld-thru or epoxy primer) before setting the rivnut to stop rust.
Install before final paint if possible, then mask threads.
inspection: Check for spinning rivnuts on high-vibration items (exhaust hangers, splash shields).

components.name: Weld-on tabs and brackets (line clamps, harness, fire system, ducts)
components.description: Small steel tabs (often with a weld nut) MIG/TIG welded to the body or cage for line clamps, harness clamps, extinguisher mounts, brake-duct hose supports and splitter/diffuser supports. Welding them on during chassis prep (before paint) is cleaner than rivnuts in many locations.
components.location: Tunnel, firewall, inner fenders, cage tubes.

raceOptions.name: Laser-cut steel tabs with captured weld nuts

installNotes: Weld all tabs before media-blasting/painting; tabs welded after paint must be re-primed.

components.name: Captured (cage) nut plates for cradle and brace bolts
components.description: The cradle and cradle-brace bolts thread into captured/caged weld nuts in the rails. A spun or stripped captured nut is a common problem on used shells. Repair by cutting an access window, welding in a new nut plate (or installing a threaded insert of equal strength), and closing the window with a doubler.
components.location: Front rails at front cradle mounts; rear rails at rear cradle mounts and cradle braces.

factory.name: GM captured weld nuts
factory.notes: Cradle bolts are torque-to-yield (74 lb ft + 90-105 deg on the rear cradle), so thread condition matters.

raceOptions.name: Weld-in nut plate / heavy-duty thread insert (e.g. Time-Sert)
raceOptions.notes: Thread repair inserts must be rated for the TTY clamp load.

installNotes: Thread-chase every captured nut before assembly; test-fit each bolt by hand to full depth.

sources.title: BMR BK061 instructions (rear cradle TAY bolts)
